source_row.rationale: An oral glucose tolerance test involves measuring blood glucose at baseline (fasting) and then at specific timed intervals (such as 1 and 2 hours, or additional intervals depending on the specific protocol) after the client ingests a standardized oral glucose solution, assessing how effectively the body processes and clears glucose over time — commonly used to screen for gestational diabetes and sometimes to help diagnose diabetes/prediabetes in non-pregnant individuals.
